valid_fixes: Restore InventoryUpdatesQueue.Properties.VisibilityTimeout to 300 so messages remain hidden for longer than the consumer Lambda's 60-second timeout
invalid_patches: Reduce SQSToDynamoDBFunction Timeout from 60 to 5 seconds — may stop re-delivery but degrades function reliability and introduces timeout errors on slow writes
Increase maxReceiveCount — does not fix re-delivery, only delays the DLQ routing
optimal_diagnostic_path: ace_check_queue_depth(queue=InventoryUpdatesQueue) → oscillates between visible=2 and in_flight=2 — messages being re-delivered repeatedly
ace_get_log_tail(function=SQSToDynamoDBFunction) → successful invocations processing same product_id and location values multiple times
ace_describe_resource(resource=SQSToDynamoDBFunction) → Timeout=60 seconds — consumer timeout exceeds visibility timeout, causing messages to re-appear before deletion
observable_symptom: Records do appear in the database (possibly duplicates). The queue never reaches zero — it continuously oscillates between showing messages visible and in-flight as the consumer repeatedly picks up and re-processes the same messages. The queue has not drained at the end of the test window.
root_cause: InventoryUpdatesQueue.VisibilityTimeout is set to 10 seconds, shorter than SQSToDynamoDBFunction.Timeout (60 seconds). When the consumer picks up messages, SQS hides them for only 10 seconds. If the invocation takes longer than 10 seconds — which occurs under LocalStack's DynamoDB write latency — SQS makes the messages visible again before the Lambda completes and deletes them. A second invocation picks them up, writing duplicate records. The queue never fully drains because messages cycle back before deletion.
